criteria.text: `term_links` exists with primary key `(days, source, person_id, a, b)` and a `person_id` foreign key with `on delete cascade`, mirroring `term_communities`'s shape.
`term_links` is in `ANALYZED_TABLES` and in `POST_BUILD_ANALYZED`, and is absent from `AGGREGATE_TABLES`.

`hasGraphAggregates()` still returns `true` after `term_links` is emptied (mirrors the existing `term_communities` test at `test/aggregate.test.ts:327-330`) — a missing or stale `term_links` never triggers a full rebuild.

For every recorte in `test/aggregate.test.ts`'s existing `recortes` table, crossed with both fixture persons, the fast `term_links` read and `linksQuery`'s live read return the identical `{s, t, count}` set (order-insensitive comparison is fine; the existing parity tests compare full `graphFor` output, so this criterion is satisfied by extending that same parity assertion to include `links`).

When `term_links` has no row for an otherwise-precomputable, built scope (e.g. after `delete from term_links where days = ... and source = ... and person_id = ...`), `graphFor` for that scope still returns the same `links` array the live `linksQuery` would produce — proving the fallback, not an empty array.

When the fast node path itself falls back to live (an unbuilt window, or a scope where `graph_terms` has no rows for that person), the links path also runs live — never a broken join where fast-links is queried against a node set the live path produced.
A window rebuild (`buildGraphAggregates`) is idempotent for `term_links`: a second build with no new docs leaves the same rows (mirrors the existing `graph_terms` idempotency test).
`test/graph.test.ts`'s `statements` map includes the new fast-links query's rendered SQL text, so its shape is pinned like every other builder in `queries`.
`GET /api/people/:id/graph`'s response for a fixed recorte, sources against `master` before this change, is byte-for-byte identical after it (a snapshot/diff check, not a new field).

Every `term_links` row for a built scope has both `a` and `b` inside that scope's linkable set `L` (definition above), and every `communityEdgesQuery` edge with both ends in `L` is present — the stored set is exactly `communityEdgesQuery ∩ (L × L)`, no more, no less.

For every recorte in the `recortes` table × both fixture persons × every `sort` × every `min` in `MINS` × `limit` ∈ {smallest, default 40, largest in `LIMITS`}, with `kind` = the full `KINDS` set, `graphFor`'s `links` equals the live `linksQuery` result — the cap never drops an edge a request can ask for.

A `graphFor` request with a narrower `kind` (e.g. `word` alone, or `word,hashtag`) on a built, precomputable scope runs `linksQuery` live and returns the live result, even when some of its edges happen to be in `term_links`.

Production size gate, checked before merge and reported in the PR body: after one full build, `pg_total_relation_size('term_links')` is at most that of `graph_terms`. If it is larger, the PR does not merge; the builder reports the number and the per-`(days, source)` row counts instead.
